subject: Discovery recap & schema/agent fit for Nimbus Payments
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir@nimbus-payments.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap & schema/agent fit for Nimbus Payments

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick written recap so we have a shared view and clear next steps. I captured the pain, target outcomes, and the specific engineering asks around tool/function calling and structured outputs.

What we heard (pain points)
- Live reconciliation latency and manual intervention across high-value merchants (~30% of support tickets are reconciliation-related).
- Current pipeline (Postgres + event workers) struggles with spike batching; dev team has limited on-call capacity for model ops.
- Need deterministic, auditable outputs for regulatory reporting (no free-form variance).

Stated goals / success criteria
- Reduce manual reconciliation work by 60% within Q1 after rollout (measured by ticket volume).
- 95% deterministic match rate for structured reconciliation actions (schema validation + idempotency).
- End-to-end latency SLO: 200–300ms p95 for single-record checks; ability to batch for bulk runs.

Current stack we discussed
- Postgres + Kafka, Go-based workers, SSO via Okta, logs in Datadog.
- No existing LLM infra on-prem; currently trialing a hosted LLM API for summarization only.

Specific asks related to tool/function calling & deterministic outputs
1) JSON schema: you asked for a rigid schema for agent outputs (action, fields, confidence, audit_id). We’ll provide a starter schema and a validation harness.
2) Tooling/agent workflow: suggested flow is (a) LLM proposes an action (JSON), (b) pre-exec validation (schema + business rules), (c) action execution by a worker with idempotency keys, (d) audit log written to an append-only store.
3) Determinism: our guidance is to pin model variant, enforce strict schema validation, and use canonical tokenization / prompt templates to avoid soft variance.

Next steps (proposed)
- I attached a draft Mutual Action Plan ("20261115-Nimbus-MAP-draft.pdf") and the call recording. Please review the MAP and confirm the timeline items we discussed.
- Samir: can you share any internal sample records and 2–3 reconciliation job examples (small CSVs) so we can sketch a concrete schema?
- We will produce a reference JSON schema and a short validation script (Python) by EOD Thursday.
- Security: you mentioned a vendor questionnaire — please send that and we’ll loop in our security PM.

If that looks right to you, I’ll schedule the follow-up technical workshop (60–90m) next week and invite Karthik and Marissa.

Thanks,
Monica Patel

From: Samir Rao <samir@nimbus-payments.com>

Subject: Re: Discovery recap & schema/agent fit for Nimbus Payments

Monica —

Thanks for the tidy recap, this matches how we took the call. A few clarifications from our side:

- Timeline: we are targeting a pilot with 5 merchant accounts by end of Q1 (Feb), so the MAP items around sandbox access and integration milestones are important.
- Security: attaching our vendor questionnaire (nimbus-security-questionnaire.pdf). We need SOC 2 in-scope artifacts and a brief on data residency for audit. Can you confirm whether Redwood can support audit log delivery to our S3 bucket?
- Determinism measures: we really need the audit_id and confidence scores per action in the JSON output — that must be surfaced to our dispute tooling.

I’ll put together the sample reconciliation CSVs (2 examples) and send them by Tuesday. Also open to the technical workshop — Wed or Thu next week works for our infra and payments teams.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Discovery recap & schema/agent fit for Nimbus Payments

Samir — appreciate the quick reply and the questionnaire. A couple of practical notes from the engineering side:

> On Sun, 15 Nov 2026 at 4:02 PM Monica Patel wrote:
> > Specific asks related to tool/function calling & deterministic outputs
> > 1) JSON schema: you asked for a rigid schema for agent outputs ...

What we can commit for the pilot
- Deliverables by end of next week: starter JSON schema (action, params, confidence, audit_id, model_version), a small validation script, and a sample mapping from your CSV columns to schema fields.
- Sandbox: we will provision a sandbox project (hosted) with api keys and a small dataset seed. That environment will have audit logs exported to an S3-compatible bucket; we support S3 destinations and can provide a signed URL process for initial ingest.
- Determinism: to minimize variance we propose using a low-temperature pinned model + response filter that rejects outputs failing schema; rejected tries will surface as structured error responses so your worker can fallback.

Workshop agenda suggestion (60–90m)
1) Walk through sample CSV -> schema mapping (15m)
2) Review JSON schema and validation rules (20m)
3) Demo a toy agent producing an action + validation + execution flow (25m)
4) Q&A + next steps / timeline (15–30m)

Can you confirm which day (Wed 11/18 or Thu 11/19) works for your infra folks? I’ll create a short agenda in Drive and link in HubSpot.
